content.title: About
content.content: Cheese ball is a small snack made from processed cheese, often enriched with spices, breadcrumbs and flavorings. It has a soft, slightly melt-in‑your‑mouth texture and a pronounced cheesy taste, making it popular with both children and adults.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Cheese balls originated in the United States in the early 20th century as a convenient snack for schoolchildren.
Typical ingredients include milk protein, vegetable oils and flavor enhancers that mimic various cheese varieties.
There are many variants: smoked, herb‑infused, cheddar, parmesan, and more.
Cheese balls are frequently included in school lunches and used as toppings for salads.

items.title: Source of calcium
items.content: Cheese balls provide calcium, which is essential for bone and tooth health.

items.title: Rich in protein
items.content: Milk protein supports tissue growth and repair.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: They contain vitamins B2 and B12, which help maintain energy metabolism.

items.title: Lactose intolerance
items.content: Cheese balls contain lactose and may cause discomfort for lactose‑intolerant individuals.

items.title: High sodium content
items.content: The product can be high in salt, which is not recommended for people with hypertension.

items.title: Milk protein allergy
items.content: Those allergic to milk proteins should avoid consumption.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Cheese balls are convenient as a stand‑alone snack, added to salads, soups, or used as a sandwich filling. They can also be warmed in the microwave for a softer texture.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store in a cool, dry place in a tightly sealed package. For longer shelf life, keep refrigerated to prevent fat oxidation.
